message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to say "See you next year!" to my teacher who's getting let go. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, this teacher, let's call him Mr. R, was new this year. From the start, he imposed his own teaching and grading methods, which were very different from what we've experienced before. Even if his methods were wrong and people pointed that out, we were still expected to follow them. That sounds pretty rigid and not open to feedback. Mr. R also took off points for scratch work he didn't like and tried to deduct as many points as possible on tests, quizzes, and homework. Every student he had was subjected to this, without exception. That seems harsh and inconsistent, especially if the grading criteria weren't clear or fair. Additionally, Mr. R took forever to grade assignments. We took a test the week before spring break and got it back about six weeks later. He also refused to go over it with anyone, which is frustrating because we didn't get any feedback or understanding of where we went wrong. Mr. R never offered help outside of the classroom and was hostile whenever asked for extra help. That's really not good because students might need additional support, and refusing to provide it can hinder their learning. The administration noticed these issues, and we were informed that Mr. R wouldn't be coming back next year. We were all overjoyed about this because his teaching style and attitude were making the school year difficult for everyone. Since the announcement, Mr. R completely checked out. He wrote notes on the board, barely talked during class, and even went to Disneyland instead of attending one of the review days for exams. It seems like he lost motivation and stopped putting effort into his job after finding out he wasn't returning. Yesterday, as I was walking out of Mr. R's classroom for the last time, I called out, "See you next year!" over my shoulder. My friends told me I'm the asshole for this, but I don't think so. I'm trying to figure out if I was right or wrong to say that. So, why did I say that? Maybe I was trying to get a reaction or make a point. Since Mr. R was letting us down and not doing his job properly, I felt justified in saying something like that. But my friends think it's mean or inappropriate. I need to consider both sides. On one hand, Mr. R's behavior was unacceptable, and he wasn't fulfilling his responsibilities as a teacher. He was rigid, harsh, and uncooperative. The administration decided he wasn't coming back, which was a relief for everyone. So, in a way, I was expressing that relief or maybe even a bit of defiance. On the other hand, saying "See you next year!" when he's not coming back could be seen as mocking or disrespectful. It might have been better to handle the situation more maturely, perhaps by not engaging in that way or by addressing the issue through the proper channels. I also need to think about the impact of my words. Did they contribute to a positive or negative environment? Did they help or hinder the situation? If my goal was to express dissatisfaction, there might be more constructive ways to do that, like talking to the administration or writing feedback. Moreover, I should consider Mr. R's feelings. Even though he wasn't doing a good job, he's still a person. Saying something like that could have been hurtful or embarrassing, especially if he was already feeling down about not returning. In the end, I need to weigh the reasons behind my actions and the consequences they had. Was it worth it to say that, or would it have been better to stay silent or address the issue differently? I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I could have expressed my feelings in a more constructive way without being disrespectful. It's important to stand up for what's right, but it's equally important to do so respectfully and maturely. Another thing to consider is the example I'm setting for others. As a student, how I handle myself in difficult situations can influence others. If I respond with disrespect, it might encourage others to do the same, which isn't helpful. Overall, I think it's a complex situation with no clear right or wrong answer. However, reflecting on the reasons behind my actions and the impact they had can help me understand whether it was appropriate or not.
